unmapped_findings: Optimized cubic lattice parameter for Fe0.5Mn0.5Al: a = b = c = 0.578 nm (Table 1).
Thermodynamic stability: cohesive energy E_coh = -6.843 eV·atom⁻¹ and formation enthalpy ΔH_r = -0.334 eV·atom⁻¹ (Table 1); both negative, indicating thermal stability.
Elastic constants (Table 2): C11 = 225.0 GPa, C12 = 152.0 GPa, C44 = 126.2 GPa. Fe0.5Mn0.5Al has the lowest C11 and C44 and the highest C12 among the Fe-containing Fe1-xMnxAl compounds.
Elastic moduli (Table 2): bulk modulus B = 176.3 GPa, shear modulus G = 77.2 GPa, Poisson's ratio σ = 0.309, B/G = 2.28 (dimensionless). B/G > 1.75 indicates ductile behavior.

Anisotropy (Table 3): universal anisotropic index A^U = 2.06, A_B = 0, A_G = 0.171, shear anisotropic factors A1 = A2 = A3 = 3.46. Fe0.5Mn0.5Al has the largest A^U among the Fe-containing compounds (strongest elastic anisotropy among them).

Bonding/metallic character: Fe0.5Mn0.5Al has the highest B/G ratio (2.28) and lowest Debye temperature (533.3 K) among the Fe-containing Fe1-xMnxAl compounds, indicating the strongest metallic character and weakest covalent bonds among them (Table 4 and text b0075).

Text statement (b0047): Fe0.5Mn0.5Al has the lowest C11 (225.0 GPa), maximum C12, minimum C44, minimum E (202.1 GPa) and maximum Poisson's ratio, which the text describes as the highest hardness and best ductility among the Fe1-xMnxAl compounds (note: Table 2 lists its H_V = 6.7 GPa, the lowest hardness value among the Fe-containing alloys).
